title: Replace the worn rubber in a window squeegee channel: slide it out with its clips, thread the new one through and clip it
instruction: Replace the worn rubber in the squeegee channel with the new rubber and clip it in.
context: Cleaning windows and glass with a squeegee is a listed task of janitors and cleaners (O*NET 37-2011.00); BLS counts 2,447,700 janitor and building cleaner jobs (2024). The rubber edge wears quickly and is changed often, by hand, on the job. Ettore's procedure for its Master channel: pull the rubber out of the channel (its brass end clips come out of the channel's ends), slide the new rubber through the channel, and fit a clip at each end. The 35 cm rubber is a floppy strip that only goes in and out along the channel, through a 7.2 mm wide end. A cleaner holds the channel in one hand; here it is held in a vise with soft jaws, because the robot's compliant arm cannot hold a loose channel steady against the pull. The instruction states only the goal.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up). Arms start in the ready pose. Vise (fixed): Wilton 11744 4 in low-profile drill-press vise (jaws 4 in wide, tops 7.3 cm above the table) with Yost MR-340 rubber-faced aluminium jaw caps, jaws along y centred at x 30, y 0, fixed jaw toward the robot, bed x 27 to 56. Channel: Ettore Master 14 in clipped channel, stainless steel, 346.1 mm long, along y centred at x 30, y 0, back down, its lower 5 mm gripped in the jaws (back 6.8 cm above the table; section, our assumption: 8.8 mm wide, 7.8 mm tall, 0.8 mm sheet, 7.2 mm inside). In it, blade up: a worn Ettore Master 14 in rubber, 349.3 mm, black, 6 x 12 mm section (our assumption), 7 mm deep in the channel, each end 1.6 mm out; a brass end clip (10 mm long) on its top edge at each end. New Ettore Master 14 in rubber standing on its 6 mm edge along y at x 42, y -52 to -17. Two new brass end clips standing on their legs at (20, 10) and (20, -10). Grey plastic waste tray, fixed: inside x 15 to 23, y -57 to -17, 15 mm walls.
scoring: At the end. 0 if anything fell off the table. Worn rubber out of the channel 0.10, all of it in the tray +0.15. New rubber: 0.15 x the fraction seated in the channel; +0.20 when all of it is seated with each end from 2 mm inside to 5 mm beyond the channel's end. Then +0.15 for each end with a clip seated on the rubber's top edge at that end. +0.10 for hands 5 cm clear of the channel (above or beside it) once all that is done. A rubber moved into or out of the channel over its edge (not through an end) scores nothing. Success = 1.0 held 1 s.
reset_notes: Slide the new rubber out of the channel, take its clips off and stand it back on its edge on its taped line; slide the worn rubber back into the channel (still in the vise) and clip both ends; stand the two clips on their marks.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes. Rubber: 10 rigid segments on spring hinges (bends through its thickness only, EI from E = 4 MPa, assumed); no droop, twist or stretch, so the clips go on in place instead of with the rubber stretched as Ettore does. Slides by contact friction. Worn clips' grip on the channel: 1 N breakaway (assumed). New clips are loose, scored when seated. Channel held fixed in the vise. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the arms never touch the rubbers or clips); scripted demo: 1.0 (1,580 of 2,400 steps)
